cards.explanation: The answer is mocking. Jeremiah says he is a laughingstock all day long and that everyone mocks him. Picture a group chat roasting you all day, and you never even joined it. I think that's a heavy way to live, friends, and Jeremiah doesn't hide it. He carries it straight to the LORD.

The answer is False. Jeremiah doesn't say the word of the LORD brought him honor. He says it has become to him “…a reproach and derision all day long.” That's blame and mockery, friends, and it follows him around all day.

The answer is a fire burning in his heart. Jeremiah says His message becomes “…a fire burning in my heart, shut up in my bones…” I know a little about heat, since my ovens run all day. But you can't shut the oven door on this one, friends. It's burning on the inside.

The answer is False. Jeremiah can't keep the message in. He says, “…I become weary of holding it in, and I cannot prevail.” He gets tired of holding it in, and he loses that tug of war. I think anyone who has tried to sit on big news knows that feeling.

The answer is his own trusted friends. Jeremiah says, “All my trusted friends watch for my fall…” These are the people he trusted. I think that's the part that stings most, friends, because it's one thing to hear it from strangers.

The word is deceived. The people watching him say, “Perhaps he will be deceived so that we may prevail against him and take our vengeance upon him.” Jeremiah used that same word about himself earlier in this passage, in verse 7. So the word is in the whispers, and it's in his own prayer too.

The answer is that they will stumble and not prevail. Jeremiah says, “…my persecutors will stumble and will not prevail.” These are the same people who were saying they would prevail against him. That's the turn, friends, because now he says they won't, since the LORD is with him like a fearsome warrior.

The answer is True. Jeremiah calls on the LORD of Hosts, “…who sees the heart and mind…” He says that right before he commits his cause to Him. I think that tells you who he wants looking at all of this, friends.

The answer is sing and praise the LORD. Jeremiah calls out, “Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD!” It comes right after he commits his cause to the LORD. After the mockery and whispering earlier in the passage, I think it's a quick swing, and I love how honest it is.

The answer is the needy. Jeremiah says the LORD “…rescues the life of the needy from the hands of evildoers.” I think he knows what it's like to feel outnumbered, so that line lands. It's a reason to praise Him that Jeremiah gives right there, friends.

The answer is False. Jeremiah says, “Cursed be the day I was born! May the day my mother bore me never be blessed.” That's a hard thing to hear, friends. I think this one hurts, and the Bible lets him say it plainly.

The answer is great joy. Jeremiah says the man brought the news to his father “bringing him great joy.” So a happy day for his dad is the very day Jeremiah is cursing. I think that makes his words even heavier, friends.

The answer is the cities the LORD overthrew. Jeremiah says, “May that man be like the cities that the LORD overthrew without compassion.” He doesn't name them here, so I won't guess which ones he means. That's the picture he gives, friends.

The answer is True. Those are Jeremiah's words, and he says the cities were ones “…that the LORD overthrew without compassion.” He says it as part of his curse, so it's his own wording in the middle of his pain. I'm only telling you what he says, friends.

The answer is trouble and sorrow. Jeremiah asks why he came out of the womb “…to see only trouble and sorrow…” It's a question, friends, and it comes straight from the heart. I think he's saying exactly how it feels.
